source_title: opengeos/RustGIS: A fast, free and open-source GIS in pure Rust. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
A fast, free and open-source GIS in pure Rust for mapping, analyzing and sharing geospatial data. Native on Windows, macOS and Linux, and in your web browser. Your data stays on your machine unless you send it to an AI model you choose, and every action is a command you can script.
Fast and small. One native program, drawn on the GPU, with no runtime to install and no server to run.
Runs everywhere. The same app on Windows, macOS and Linux, and compiled to WebAssembly at web.rustgis.app with nothing to install.
Local and private. Your files are read and written on your machine, and nothing is uploaded on its own. The network is used only when you ask for it: web basemaps, plugins, the GeoLibre tools and the AI model you pick, which receives your questions and the data it reads to answer them.
Everything is a command. Every button in the ribbon is a command with an id. Script it from rustgis-cli , chain it in notebooks and models, use completion in the Script pane, or ask the AI Assistant to run it for you.
Familiar. A ribbon laid out in the order of the work (Home, Data, Style, Edit, Analyze, View, Publish), Layers and Browser panes, an attribute table, and undo for every change.
Extensible. Over 1,000 GeoLibre and Whitebox tools for terrain, hydrology, LiDAR and remote sensing, and sandboxed WebAssembly plugins that add commands, tools and ribbon tabs.
Symbology and tables. Graduated colours, with the selection synced to the table.
AI Assistant. Ask about your data or tell the map what to do.
Analysis. A tool gallery, the Tools pane and 1,000+ GeoLibre tools.
Rasters. GeoTIFF and COG, with stretch, RGB and shaded-relief styles.
Globe and projections. A 3D globe, Equal Earth, Robinson or any EPSG code.
Web basemaps. XYZ, WMS and vector tiles, and MapLibre styles.
Layouts. Map frames, legends, scale bars, map series and PDF export.
Plugins. Install sandboxed plugins from plugins.rustgis.app .
ModelBuilder. Chain tools on a node canvas and run them in one go.
Web Data. STAC, Overture Maps, NASA and open-data portals, where the map is.
Terrain. Tilt the map and drape it over elevation.
Other worlds. The Moon, Mars and nine more bodies, on their own basemaps.
Extrusion. Stand features up by a field, lit and shaded.
Time Slider. Step dated features and imagery through time.
Dark mode and the View tab's effects, panes and linked views.
Projects. Start blank, from the World Atlas sample, or open a project.
Every screenshot is RustGIS itself, rendered offscreen by cargo run -p rustgis-ui-egui --example ui_shot .
The user guide covers each area in detail, Comparison sets RustGIS beside GeoLibre, QGIS and ArcGIS, and ROADMAP.md lists what's next.
Web app : open web.rustgis.app . The same ribbon and tools, with the browser's file picker for data and projects, and downloads for Save and Export.
Desktop : download the app for Windows, macOS or Linux from downloads.rustgis.app or the latest release (see Installation for the files and first-run notes).
Microsoft Store : get RustGIS from the Microsoft Store on Windows 10 and 11, which installs it in one click and keeps it up to date.
Package managers : winget install OpenGeos.RustGIS , brew install --cask opengeos/rustgis/rustgis , yay -S rustgis-bin (AUR), or sudo dnf copr enable giswqs/rustgis && sudo dnf install rustgis (Fedora).
From source : cargo run --release -p rustgis (Rust 1.90 or later).
Command line: every ribbon action is a command with an id.
Python: the same engine and commands in-process ( pip install rustgis ), and the app itself in a Jupyter notebook.
See Python and the getting-started notebook ( open in Colab ).
Layered crates, each depending only on the ones below it:
cargo xtask ci runs formatting, clippy, the tests and the layering check. Contributor and agent notes: AGENTS.md .
RustGIS is free and open source, and stays that way. If it is useful to you or your team, sponsorship is the most direct way to keep development, hosting and cross-platform distribution going.
GitHub Sponsors : monthly or one-time, billed through your GitHub account.
Buy Me a Coffee : a quick one-off contribution, no account required.
See the Become a Sponsor page for what sponsorship supports and for other, free ways to help.
If you use RustGIS in your work, please cite it. RustGIS is archived on Zenodo , which mints a DOI for every release. The concept DOI below always resolves to the latest version.
Wu, Q., Rincón Albarracín, J. G., Filho, E., Hofbauer, D., Fitzgerald, M., & Strebel, D. (2026). RustGIS: A fast, free and open-source GIS in pure Rust for mapping, analyzing and sharing geospatial data. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23633281
You can also use GitHub's "Cite this repository" button (which reads CITATION.cff ) to copy a ready-made APA or BibTeX entry. See the How to Cite page for more formats.
RustGIS builds on the work of many projects and their authors: QGIS , ArcGIS Pro and GDAL , the GIS it is measured against; MapLibre and PROJ ; the GeoLibre tool suite, after John Lindsay's WhiteboxTools ; OpenFreeMap for vector basemaps; Natural Earth , OpenStreetMap , Overture Maps and the EPSG dataset; and the Rust crates it is made of, among them egui , wgpu , tiny-skia , geo , proj4rs , tiff , Apache Arrow and Parquet, rusqlite and wasmi . See the acknowledgements for the full list, and ATTRIBUTION.md for every asset's source and licence.
RustGIS is primarily built with Claude Opus 5.5 , an AI model by Anthropic, working under human direction and review. Its results are tested, but check them for your own use, and please report anything that looks wrong.
